query: Walk me through a year-by-year glide path that gradually shifts my allocation over the next decade.

recommendations.title: Implement 10-Year Retirement Glide Path (Ages 55-65)
recommendations.summary: Execute a systematic de-risking strategy that gradually reduces equity exposure from 55% to 35% while increasing bond allocation from 35% to 55% over the next decade, with annual rebalancing milestones.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Given your current age of 55 and retirement target at 65, a structured glide path is essential to protect accumulated wealth while maintaining growth potential. Your current allocation (55% equity/35% bonds/5% cash/5% alternatives) is appropriate for age 55 with moderate risk tolerance. The recommended path: Year 1 (Age 55): 55/35/5/5; Year 2-3 (Ages 56-57): 52/37/6/5; Year 4-5 (Ages 58-59): 48/40/7/5; Year 6-7 (Ages 60-61): 44/44/7/5; Year 8-9 (Ages 62-63): 40/48/7/5; Year 10 (Age 64): 35/53/7/5; Retirement (Age 65): 35/55/10/0. This gradual 2% equity reduction every 1-2 years minimizes sequence-of-returns risk while keeping you invested for growth. The final 35/55/10 allocation supports your $80-100k income goal (approximately 4-4.5% withdrawal rate from projected $1.8M portfolio) while maintaining purchasing power against inflation. Begin by establishing target bands and calendar reminders for annual reviews each January.
recommendations.suggested_action: Establish annual rebalancing schedule with year-by-year targets; immediately document current 55/35/5/5 baseline; set calendar reminder for January 2026 review to shift toward 52/37/6/5

recommendations.title: Add Intermediate-Term Bond Fund for Glide Path Execution
recommendations.summary: Introduce BIV (Vanguard Intermediate-Term Bond ETF) or similar to create bond ladder structure supporting the gradual shift from 35% to 55% fixed income allocation while managing interest rate risk.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current bond allocation relies heavily on BND (total bond market), which has average duration of 6-7 years. As you increase bond exposure from 35% to 55% over the next decade, concentration in a single bond duration creates interest rate risk. Adding intermediate-term bonds (3-5 year duration) creates a more resilient fixed income structure. Recommended bond sub-allocation evolution: Currently 35% bonds (all BND) → Target by Age 60: 40% bonds (25% BND + 15% BIV) → Target by Age 65: 55% bonds (30% BND + 20% BIV + 5% short-term). This laddered approach provides: 1) Reduced volatility through duration diversification, 2) Natural rebalancing as bonds mature, 3) Stable income stream for retirement transition. Begin building BIV position with 10% of portfolio (approximately $85k) over next 12 months through systematic rebalancing, sourcing funds from equity reduction as glide path progresses.
recommendations.suggested_action: Initiate 10% position in intermediate-term bond ETF (BIV preferred) over next 6-12 months; fund through natural rebalancing from equity positions

recommendations.title: Reduce Individual Stock Concentration to Support Glide Path
recommendations.summary: Decrease individual stock holdings (JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B, PG) from 15% to 10% of portfolio over next 24 months, reinvesting proceeds into bond positions to support de-risking trajectory.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your 15% allocation to individual stocks (concentrated in 5 holdings) creates unnecessary idiosyncratic risk as you approach retirement. While these are quality companies, individual stock positions increase volatility and sequence-of-returns risk during the critical decade before retirement. Your advanced investment experience has served you well, but the glide path requires reducing concentrated positions. Recommend: Year 1 (Age 55-56): Reduce individual stocks from 15% to 12.5% (~$21k reduction) → Year 2 (Age 56-57): Further reduce to 10% (~$21k additional) → Age 60+: Maintain 5-7% maximum. This systematic reduction accomplishes three objectives: 1) Lowers portfolio volatility by 8-12% based on historical correlations, 2) Provides capital for bond allocation increases without disrupting core ETF positions (VTI/VXUS), 3) Reduces tax-loss harvesting complexity in retirement. Prioritize selling positions with smallest conviction or those near cost basis to minimize tax impact. Your healthcare overweight (22% via JNJ/UNH) is already captured in VTI; reducing overlap improves true diversification.
recommendations.suggested_action: Trim individual stock positions from 15% to 12.5% within next 12 months; reinvest proceeds into BND and BIV to advance glide path; target final 10% allocation by age 57

recommendations.title: Maintain Core VTI/VXUS Equity Foundation Through Glide Path
recommendations.summary: Preserve VTI and VXUS as primary equity vehicles throughout the 10-year glide path, adjusting only total equity allocation while maintaining 70/30 US/international split within equity portion.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your core equity holdings (VTI for US exposure, VXUS for international diversification) are optimal vehicles for glide path execution and should remain your equity foundation. As overall equity allocation decreases from 55% to 35%, maintain consistent 70% US/30% international split within the equity portion (currently approximately this ratio given VTI dominance). This approach provides: 1) Low-cost, broad diversification (VTI holds 3,500+ US stocks, VXUS covers 7,000+ international), 2) Tax efficiency through ETF structure during accumulation and de-accumulation phases, 3) Simplified rebalancing with just two equity positions versus multiple funds. Specific targets: Age 55: 38.5% VTI + 16.5% VXUS = 55% total equity → Age 60: 33.6% VTI + 14.4% VXUS = 48% total equity → Age 65: 24.5% VTI + 10.5% VXUS = 35% total equity. Never sell these positions completely; the 35% equity allocation at retirement provides inflation protection and supports 30+ year retirement horizon. Review annually but resist tactical changes; your glide path IS your strategy.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold and maintain as core equity positions; adjust position sizes only per annual glide path schedule; maintain ~70/30 US/international ratio within total equity allocation
